thread:
sophie: Quick sync idea — proposing a "split-control" model for tenant-managed egress and upgrade-safe routing for Private. Goal: let customers own egress nat/ip but keep control-plane fallback and safe rollback. Thoughts?

aj: +1 for concept. need to spell out launch gates. what does "split-control" actually mean in config terms?

pavan: Roughly: control plane manages model/catalog & rollout policies; tenant owns egress and BGP NAT. runtime has a narrow fallback mode to our relay if tenant connectivity breaks. main engineering work: installer flags + health probes + connection backoff logic.

maria: Field ask: customers want the ability to change egress IPs without a full operator upgrade. also they need a deterministic rollback window for upgrades (30m-2h). If we can expose a simple knob, that'll help a bunch.

sean: Security note: tenant-managed egress requires us to enforce mTLS and cert pinning on control-plane channels. fallback relay must not leak customer metadata. also confirm KMS/HSM integration for onprem keys.

aj: Launch criteria proposal: 1) Installer flag --egress=tenant|relay 2) Healthcheck + circuit-breaker default (3 failed checks -> relay) 3) Integration test: simulated network partition + automatic fallback recovery 4) Telemetry: egress-ip, fallback-count, time-to-reconnect 5) Docs & field runbook.

pavan: Implementation sketch (config snippet):
```
# /etc/redwood/config.yaml
control_plane:
  endpoint: https://control.redwood.example
  cert_pinning: true
runtime:
  egress_mode: tenant   # tenant | relay
  fallback: enabled
  fallback_threshold: 3
  fallback_window_s: 300
```
This is intentionally small so operators can patch quickly.

maria: Can we add a soft-requirement: customers must provide an "admin callback" URL for upgrade notifications? Helps field automate maintenance windows.

sophie: yes, include admin_callback optional field in onboarding. For prioritization: propose we do an initial alpha for Dedicated customers in Q2, then wider Private customers in Q3. P0 checks: safe rollback, no secret exfil, and minimal installer changes.

aj: Risk list: 1) unexpected NAT churn during canary -> client IP changes break licensing 2) edge cases with IPv6 + dual-stack 3) operator error flipping egress mode mid-upgrade -> must be a no-op or require explicit confirm. Need gating e2e tests.

sean: For licensing/identity, suggest we emit a stable "runtime-id" (rotate on reinstall only) so downstream infra can map traffic even if egress ip changes. encrypt runtime-id with customer KMS.

pavan: Agreed. Also we should add a migration step for existing installs: if egress_mode missing -> default to relay to avoid surprise. Migration doc + k8s annotation that marks manual opt-in.

ops-bot: Action items created: RD-1429 (split-control spec doc), RD-1430 (installer flag spike), RD-1431 (e2e partition test). Owners: @aj RD-1429/1430, @pavan RD-1431.

sophie: Next steps: aj and pavan assemble a 1-pager with the config, test plan, and field rollout phasing. maria to collect 3 customer use-cases for early alpha. Sean will draft a short security checklist. Can we reconvene Thu 10am?

aj: Thu 10 works. I'll put a short agenda: goals, acceptance tests, minimal UX for opt-in.

maria: I'll ping two customers and bring notes.

sophie: thanks all. keeping this tight will help ship with minimal surprise. :thumbsup:
